steps.why: Every command on PATH has a page, which is text: its first line is no macro. The loop prints the names that failed.
steps.script: rm -f /tmp/pageless; for file in /bin/* /usr/bin/*; do test -e "$file" || continue; name=${file##*/}; man "$name" > /tmp/page && sed 1q /tmp/page | grep -qv '^[.]' || echo "$name" >> /tmp/pageless; done; ! cat /tmp/pageless 2> /dev/null

steps.why: Dolly's own pages are their --help, where upstream's begin with their title, NAME(1); test and [ take --help as an expression, echo as an operand. Each program runs by its path: command and time are Slop's own too.
steps.script: rm -f /tmp/helpless; for file in /bin/* /usr/bin/*; do name=${file##*/}; if test -e "/usr/share/man/cat1/$name.1" && ! sed 1q "/usr/share/man/cat1/$name.1" | grep -q '^[A-Z].*([1-9])' && test "$name" != test && test "$name" != "[" && test "$name" != echo; then "$file" --help > /tmp/help && test -s /tmp/help || echo "$name" >> /tmp/helpless; fi; done; ! cat /tmp/helpless 2> /dev/null

steps.why: help is the first thing the greeting names: it fits a terminal of 80 columns.
Upstream's pages are formatted when the image is built.
steps.script: man grep > /tmp/page && grep -q '^NAME' /tmp/page && grep -q 'search files for patterns' /tmp/page && ! grep -Eq '^[.](Dd|Nm|Sh) ' /tmp/page

steps.why: A command without a page is 1, said on standard error only.
A misuse is 2, said on standard error only.
A package's pages arrive with it.

steps.script: amy install git && man git > /tmp/page && git --help > /tmp/help && cmp /tmp/page /tmp/help
